To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we performed the first genome-wide association study of personality factors in a family-based sample of centenarians and found two significant SNPs that reached genome-wide significance.

1) a genome-wide association analysis of the personality traits of agreeableness in a large sample of individuals from the Long Life Family study, a sample enriched in longevity, identified a SNP that was genome-wide significantly associated with this personality trait; 2) this association was not replicated in an independent cohort; 3) the genome-wide association analysis identified several SNPs that were associated with personality traits, but the associations did not reach genome-wide significance.
three SNPs in almost perfect LD associated with agreeabeness in the LLFS sample reached genome-wide significance, and that the associations did not replicate in two additional samples.
In summary, our research is concerned with
genetic factors that influence personality and may be involved with longevity.
the genetic basis of personality traits as related to longevity, and we have identified several novel SNPs and age-by-SNP interaction that are associated with agreeabeness.
the identification of genetic factors associated with personality traits and longevity, which may be relevant for the understanding of healthy aging and longevity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

no genome-wide significant associations were observed in the LLFS GWAS of personality traits, but several marginal associations were observed, and the possibility of complex gene–gene interaction could be considered.
no genome-wide significant association of SNPs was found for personality traits in the LLFS cohort, but some SNPs reached marginal significance.

the genome-wide significant association of rs9650241 with agreeableness was replicated, while the genome-wide significant associations of rs9650239 and rs9650242 with agreeableness failed to be replicated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GWAS for personality traits in the LLFS identified novel SNPs and age-by-SNP interaction effects.
we identified a number of SNPs associated with personality traits, but we did not replicate any association that reached genome-wide significance.
the genetic factors associated with personality traits are different from those previously reported in the literature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
personality traits are heritable, and the genetic variants associated with personality traits are likely to be the same in the general population as in LLFS subjects.
the genetic architecture underlying personality traits is complex and requires a large sample size to be fully characterized.

the genetic architecture of personality traits, as measured by NEO-five-factor, is complex, and that it is unlikely that one SNP or a few genes will account for a substantial proportion of the variance in personality traits.
